transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It does not sound like a motor that is about to fail. A failing motor normally remains noisy regardless of surface, often with a rough whine, grinding or screeching. Becoming louder on a rug, using more battery, then settling again on tiles is much more consistent with the vacuum increasing suction because the rug creates more resistance and/or contains more dust. The changing screen may also be normal display activity: it can change as the vacuum senses dust and adjusts its response. The useful distinction is whether it is changing its displayed information normally, or actually switching modes without you touching the controls. 1. Check which power mode is selected. In Auto/medium, a change in motor note and quicker battery use on carpet can be normal. In Boost/Max it will drain much faster on any surface.
2. With the vacuum switched off, remove the floorhead and clear hair or thread from the brush bar. Check the roller turns freely by hand. A partly jammed roller or restricted airway can make it work harder on a rug.
3. Also check the bin inlet, wand and floorhead neck for debris, and make sure the filter is clean, fully dry and seated correctly. A restriction usually causes persistent louder running, pulsing, loss of pickup, or warning messages—not just a temporary change between hard floor and rug. As it is only around four months old, report it under the guarantee if it is genuinely changing power modes by itself, the display is flickering or restarting, it becomes loud on all surfaces, pulses/cuts out, smells hot, or gives a blockage/filter warning after those basic checks. A video showing the screen and sound while moving from tiles to the rug is useful evidence for Dyson.

I checked the screen and it says 'Auto'. I changed it from Eco to that about two weeks ago, which is when I first noticed this. The brush bar is clean with no hair on it, the wand is clear when I look down it, and I washed the filter last month and let it dry for a day. There's no burning smell, heat or sparks, and no warnings or red lights on the screen. Does 'Auto' explain what I'm hearing?

Yes. Auto mode is the most likely explanation for the louder motor and faster fall in the battery estimate on the rug. In Auto, the vacuum can raise and lower suction as it detects a heavier cleaning load; a rug commonly creates more resistance and may hold more fine dust than tiles. When you return to the tiles, it eases back again. That pattern is not typical of a suction motor failing. The screen moving up and down is also likely normal if it is the dust/bar-graph or remaining-run-time information changing. The important distinction is whether the mode label remains “Auto”, or whether the vacuum is actually changing mode by itself. If it stays labelled Auto and simply gets louder on the rug before settling on tiles, I would treat that as normal operation rather than report a motor fault. If the label changes to Eco/Boost without button presses, the screen flickers/restarts, or it becomes noisy on hard floors too, record a short video and contact Dyson under the guarantee.

candidates: Normal automatic suction adjustment and display activity on a higher-resistance rug (high)
Partly restricted floorhead, brush bar or airflow (medium)
